All five are implemented in `problems.py`, standard library only, signatures and docstrings untouched.

- **`parse_duration`** — single anchored regex `(?:(\d+)h)?(?:(\d+)m)?(?:(\d+)s)?\Z` with `re.ASCII`. Ordering, duplicate units, bare units, whitespace, signs, and trailing garbage all fail to match; the all-empty match is rejected by an explicit "at least one component" check. `\Z` (not `$`) rejects a trailing newline, and `re.ASCII` rejects non-ASCII digits like `"١h"`. Non-`str` input raises `ValueError`.
- **`luhn_valid`** — strips spaces/hyphens, returns `False` for empty/non-digit (explicit ASCII digit set, so `str.isdigit()` quirks like `"²"` or Arabic-Indic digits don't slip through), then doubles every second digit from the right. `"0"` → valid, other single digits → invalid. Never raises, including on non-string input.
- **`flatten`** — recursive walk into a fresh output dict; input is never touched. Empty nested dicts contribute nothing at any depth; lists and other non-dict values pass through by reference. Uses a `None` prefix sentinel so an empty-string key still nests correctly (`{"": {"x": 1}}` → `{".x": 1}`).
- **`top_k_frequent`** — `Counter` plus `sorted` on `(-count, word)`; `k <= 0` → `[]`, oversized `k` naturally truncates to all distinct words.
- **`rolling_max`** — monotonic-deque of indices, O(n) with one pass and no `max()` per window. `window <= 0` raises `ValueError`; `window > len(nums)` returns `[]`.

I verified with a throwaway script (since deleted) covering the docstring examples plus the edge cases above, cross-checked `rolling_max` against a brute-force `max()` reference on 300k random ints across several window sizes. Timing there: 0.108s for 300k elements at window 5000.
